dedupe_keys.name: our lady of lourdes memorial hospital floodwall retrofit binghamton new york

description: This case describes how a community hospital on the bank of the Susquehanna River in Binghamton, New York, protected itself from repeated flooding with a floodwall. Our Lady of Lourdes Memorial Hospital, a 197-bed facility in the FEMA 100-year floodplain, was flooded in June 2006 when water overtopped an earthen berm and covered the ground floor with 16 to 20 inches of contaminated water, damaging the power plant, backup generators, fuel tanks and water supply, causing $20 million in damage and forcing evacuation of all 150 patients. Having just spent $70 million on modernisation, the hospital worked with FEMA, state emergency management and environmental agencies and the Army Corps of Engineers on a mitigation plan funded by FEMA Hazard Mitigation Assistance: a 1,365-foot concrete T-wall built to the 500-year flood elevation, 11 automatic floodgates, stop logs, interior drainage and pumping, and relocated utilities. The provider is the New York State Climate Impacts Assessment, which publishes it as a case study. Coverage is one hospital site. In September 2011 Tropical Storm Lee produced a flood above the 2006 record that damaged over 2,000 buildings in Binghamton, yet the hospital stayed fully operational. The page is available free online as a web page, with no licence stated, and cites FEMA sources. Caveats: costs of the wall are not given, and outcomes come from FEMA and assessment summaries. Simulation uses: comparing protect-in-place and relocation options in hospital flood adaptation models. Related records: the New Orleans Veterans Affairs rebuild (case_study-new-orleans-va-hospital-flood-resilient-rebuild) chose elevation instead.
